productCodes.reason: Hall of Beorn numbers The Dark of Mirkwood's cards 02001 to 02051, which are the codes RingsDB gives The Hunt for Gollum (02004 is Winged Guardian and also Surprise Attack). RingsDB lists the nine burden, boon and adaptation cards of the box as 41041 to 41049 (Stalking Goblin is 02041 in Hall of Beorn and 41041 in RingsDB). The code is therefore 410 and the two-digit collector number, for every card of the box, so the quest, encounter and campaign cards RingsDB does not list take the same pattern (After the Raid 41001, The Oath 41050).
productCodes.source: hallofbeorn.com/Export/EncounterCards, QuestCards, PlayerCards (CardSet The Dark of Mirkwood, Number); ringsdb.com pack TDoM (41041 to 41049)

productCodes.reason: Hall of Beorn codes the Dream-chaser Campaign Expansion '12' and the collector number (13 to 217), which are the codes of the six Adventure Packs' own cards (12013 Full Sail Ahead, 12063 Scouting Party, 12138 Prince Imrahil) and of Ered Mithrin (12166 to 12204). RingsDB codes the box's boons and burdens 11172 to 11216, one gap per campaign card. A card with collector number 171 or more (the nine campaign cards, the 37 boons and burdens, the Hard and Expert Mode card) is therefore '11' and its number, which is RingsDB's code where RingsDB lists it and the same pattern where it does not (campaign cards 11171, 11179, 11182, 11191, 11194, 11197, 11200, 11209, 11215; Hard and Expert Mode 11217).

productCodes.reason: A Dream-chaser Campaign Expansion card with a collector number below 171 is a 2023 reprint of a card the Adventure Packs print (Calphon 13, the Stormcaller 42, The Thing in the Depths 63, Temple Guardian 77, Gate Key 78, Dol Amroth Warship 102, the Shattered Monument 129, the six ships 136 to 141) with a Campaign Mode only or Upgraded side. Its Hall of Beorn code ('12' and the number) is the original's, so it is '110' and its three-digit number (110042 is the Stormcaller reprint; 12019 is the pack's). The six-digit prefix 110 is unused; the other six-digit prefixes are 131-132, 140-148 and 900-907. The two sides of one reprint share the code.

productCodes.reason: Hall of Beorn codes the Ered Mithrin Campaign Expansion '19' and the collector number (165 to 204), which collides with six Fate of Wilderland codes (19165 to 19170). RingsDB codes the box's 31 boons, burdens and treasures '12' and its collector number (12166 to 12204), which no other card bears, so a card with number 166 or more takes that code, and the eight campaign cards RingsDB does not list take the same pattern (Lost in Mirkwood 12168, The King's Quest 12170, The Withered Heath 12175, Roam Across Rhovanion 12184, Fire in the Night 12187, The Ghost of Framsburg 12189, Mount Gundabad 12193, The Fate of Wilderland 12195).

productCodes.reason: Hall of Beorn and RingsDB number the box's cards one above the collector number the cards print (the scans print 164 on Journey Up the Anduin, 166 on A Growing Threat, 167 on Lost in Mirkwood), and the code follows their number. The Journey Up the Anduin campaign card is their number 165, and '12165' is Fury and Malice of The City of Corsairs (RingsDB, pack CoC; 12164 is Umbar Patrol). The six-digit prefix 120 is unused (the prefixes in use are 110, 131-132, 140-148 and 900-907), so the card is 120165.

dragnPackAliases.reason: DragnCards' load lists for Journey Up the Anduin and Lost in Mirkwood (Q08.1, Q08.2) deal the 2011 Core Set's cards of the Wilderlands, Journey Along the Anduin, Passage Through Mirkwood, Spiders of Mirkwood and Dol Guldur Orcs sets. The Ered Mithrin Campaign Expansion's setup text names the same sets, and the app already builds and ledgers them as the Revised Core Set's reprints (same codes 01074 to 01131, same collector numbers), so a Core Set row is the Revised Core Set card with its collector number and name (user decision, 2026-11-05).

dragnCardCodes.reason: Wormsbane is one card with two sides, Broken (side A) and Reforged (side B), and DragnCards files it as one Attachment card with a .B picture, collector number 143. Hall of Beorn files the two sides as two Objective cards, #143 Wormsbane (Broken) and #144 Wormsbane (Reforged), so no title and type match finds either (the Setup line is "Attach Wormsbane to a hero, Broken side face-up"). Side A is the Broken card.

dragnCardCodes.reason: Abandoned Village is an objective-location of Lost in Mirkwood. DragnCards types it Location, and Hall of Beorn has no OCTGN guid for it (its three siblings Overgrown Path, Bare Hilltop and Forest Clearing have one), so no guid or type match finds it. encounterSetAliases.reason: The Revised Core Set's Learn to Play (p25) and the Easy Mode sheet (p2) call the second core scenario and its encounter set "Journey Down the Anduin". The scenario's own campaign card, quest cards and encounter set icon print "Journey Along the Anduin" (Mirkwood Paths - Part 2, scan 01130.A), and Hall of Beorn follows the cards. The card wins (authority order); the booklet's name is an alias.
